macronutrients, ingredient lists, and percent daily values have become the
[primary language of
eating](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BNT9Urk6XmPubSyDNsyeJwVRSCYGRC-2Fv-2BNa9IbDRFTFIlg8Ojn8VSiA7eHu0B-2F-2BRew-3D-3Doqor_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BBb8InrSWScXWwwhR8KaNc47rVfyD1XCoa6i59gYLZ9oZIF2-2B57xGvBAIKJX7TG6Hcwua22EO2819LZprpDEx2227d8PHa0Dxn3I1PMgOqFrVkTkNst5jeawcb-2FfLcaeQFqjSrQWI2TK7n1t3tRdydfsyyTzLRZImgGKMmiWc754v-2B2po1Mlgpeoy72c7b-2FIG-2B8W7cfGANLrsIwLVi1k-2BGX9kvTIFsWcB8LGgcXN5wArHpwuN3tKlYUV0PXLVDikSarWHFRcEwxztnEdE93ajUYlWHL0JgffBtxLZpy35H6Xauo1Yt0FOitg6jX4dUXYxEeEaX5cg5w-2Bmgmy3YkoESVLJXb2VM5XKrSs-2Bmutna1vTcGVv4mHteZYaZd02YNqTiQlXAY5K6vIycJHaaaDeqnnM4sJL60k-2FPE3-2BJgy04oy63PljqsB9ENh2AweILdUcRTRuJK3VcMgGrNiYtsjyhSWiqXaASbRswGltDpgAxMN3VA03-2F8nSXt3gcwwpUvbyftSlC6RxVZROMLpHUXjuIbsBsQ5Q7zIZIO2SK4Kw8VIlfrlMlZvXmGC66a9DbWyKDqCIgUy87E3gcgYYP-2FSjKu3l87ZuqIRUODP7r7HmxUrm2dP2-2FSRTQDPCI3T2a0-2BxyaOQjEfMwPEZePvvzVtJnF0-2BLOAPLDyLf3wUNR87TR77z0PzURf106qkJGc-2BFdmNexHM1wCiOfY9xh35gPfFEOO-2F5X3Vz1fWBJdNoi-2F-2FgWRP3Z206-2FHXviJk8Hpa4QnN).

assumes that the effects of the food we consume can be understood by breaking
it down into isolated components and optimizing those components. If the label
looks right, the thinking goes, good health should follow.

But human experience tells a different story. Food is not just fuel; it is not
merely a list of nutrients. Meals carry aroma, texture, memory, and meaning.
Cultural traditions shape how foods are prepared, combined, and shared.
Emotional states influence appetite and response. These elements are not
superfluous add-ons to dietary health; they are part of how the body
interprets what we eat.

Increasingly, modern science supports this lived reality. Foods that appear
equivalent based on nutrition labels can produce [very different
outcomes](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BOfNE-2Fr4d42hklKAzvg0qXQJ0IG9mKZUAe5UKtKjgqrdmX3qMMnsHTtBasAcZAXn-2FhILjnYQ41Ox0wjiNbyRn-2FYfKOuSuNH1QAYltIKk-2F-2FXz8541Uiwblnt2fGqxPW0JAbPVisgVNuhupOgSrPSnzQM7TFN2oKYWwNnAkSOD9rBQvjd83XCSEcF4gc1xy3dWgZLzRMmXSgNydI6P0pgKi95AXyjaCNa3V0QXX37lfgDK-2FCHD5Tb-2F72anK-2BV9lInuDw-3D-3Dd3b4_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BBb8InrSWScXWwwhR8KaNc47rVfyD1XCoa6i59gYLZ9oZIF2-2B57xGvBAIKJX7TG6Hcwua22EO2819LZprpDEx2227d8PHa0Dxn3I1PMgOqFrVkTkNst5jeawcb-2FfLcaeQFqjSrQWI2TK7n1t3tRdydfsyyTzLRZImgGKMmiWc754v-2B2po1Mlgpeoy72c7b-2FIG-2B8W7cfGANLrsIwLVi1k-2BGX9kvTIFsWcB8LGgcXN5wArHpwuN3tKlYUV0PXLVDikSarWHFRcEwxztnEdE93ajUYlWHL0JgffBtxLZpy35H6Xauo1Yt0FOitg6jX4dUXYxEeEaX5cg5w-2Bmgmy3YkoESVLJXb2VM5XKrSs-2Bmutna1vTcGVv4mHteZYaZd02YNqTiQlXAY5K6vIycJHaaaDeqnnM4sJL60k-2FPE3-2BJgy04oy63PljqsB9ENh2AweILdUcRTRuJK3VcMgGrNiYtsjyhSWiqXaASbRswGltDpgAxMN3VA03-2F8nSXt3gcwwpUvbyftSlC6RxVZROMLpHUXjuIbsBsQ5Q7zIZIO2SK4Kw8VKeXjbx3FVByiA7MxIlwh7EzXYLfNxuf5fv4FtwRJM-2Bz4ps6pNk-2FmovuyCoO1CoIjLEFmq8R7G8Fq1aXm-2B0mVNTpXx4MCrDY8-2BNz2xXAOlyFODxyzpnTPvNdtdViFHE5qcIPMbZuUVHquDDlJtcmagVVx-2FegjltG1MRRtLcGqxFr6wAh0eErYF49imsT1lW-2FdsNfggnAG-2BCWmU5XjE2UD1N)
depending on when we eat, as well as the structure, content, context, and
prior exposure. The body does not simply absorb nutrients; it responds to [
_patterns of
signals_](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BJMjy53vIeK4iV7SvML7ndRPtNM9zl4dKlezW6Rl8nG6In8Ej3Oj9MCoTw3V4VL9fbDRtdXgHh80vGccCQfpJYRgPR8JCYmaMRzYVqd4U617Pr5jQ7DHPFR5GaN-2BX3EUMQ-3D-3Ddpe4_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BBb8InrSWScXWwwhR8KaNc47rVfyD1XCoa6i59gYLZ9oZIF2-2B57xGvBAIKJX7TG6Hcwua22EO2819LZprpDEx2227d8PHa0Dxn3I1PMgOqFrVkTkNst5jeawcb-2FfLcaeQFqjSrQWI2TK7n1t3tRdydfsyyTzLRZImgGKMmiWc754v-2B2po1Mlgpeoy72c7b-2FIG-2B8W7cfGANLrsIwLVi1k-2BGX9kvTIFsWcB8LGgcXN5wArHpwuN3tKlYUV0PXLVDikSarWHFRcEwxztnEdE93ajUYlWHL0JgffBtxLZpy35H6Xauo1Yt0FOitg6jX4dUXYxEeEaX5cg5w-2Bmgmy3YkoESVLJXb2VM5XKrSs-2Bmutna1vTcGVv4mHteZYaZd02YNqTiQlXAY5K6vIycJHaaaDeqnnM4sJL60k-2FPE3-2BJgy04oy63PljqsB9ENh2AweILdUcRTRuJK3VcMgGrNiYtsjyhSWiqXaASbRswGltDpgAxMN3VA03-2F8nSXt3gcwwpUvbyftSlC6RxVZROMLpHUXjuIbsBsQ5Q7zIZIO2SK4Kw8VLfoUnsCMnNk4zX6fWbILORN24f4jxSMZg-2FqA9yuj4sCcj1UZeEOxewBuMwGxEY9DQNo1oTKJ0YtQTSm-2FMzp-2Fgx0seBq9en9-2FttB43pBLDTl69-2FRJbKmg7OiajYraQO-2BUud85GpWxZF5uTuFrY8SDm0UWc-2FNevZpZYeVNh184BG-2Fc97QyE3e44E-2BvWf-2F6JuA79Pe4mjEkIrU8Hgjrl6qrcw)
shaped by experience and environment.

From this perspective, food does not simply function as fuel or as random
nutrients, but as  _information_ —signals that biological systems interpret
and respond to. It communicates simultaneously with metabolism, hormones,
microbes, and behavior. Health does not emerge from perfect labels or isolated
nutrients, but from the relationships between how these signals are organized
over time. Moving beyond nutritionism does not abandon science—it strengthens
it by aligning prevailing models of nutrition—such as calorie-based energy
balance and nutrient reductionism, with how living organisms actually exist as
complex adaptive systems.

**When Food Became Fuel: The Origins of Nutrition’s Numbers**

Modern nutrition’s fascination with numbers did not begin with health. It
began with economics.

heat](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BESpJ0iZAPMCfF4sYQ9QHS2rvbj2VJ1YsfxX43oTodLgZaZ8xjEyThSLJxuXXfWI8Klb2D-2BAjh3Knf1SpWVfXmI-3DCD_v_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BBb8InrSWScXWwwhR8KaNc47rVfyD1XCoa6i59gYLZ9oZIF2-2B57xGvBAIKJX7TG6Hcwua22EO2819LZprpDEx2227d8PHa0Dxn3I1PMgOqFrVkTkNst5jeawcb-2FfLcaeQFqjSrQWI2TK7n1t3tRdydfsyyTzLRZImgGKMmiWc754v-2B2po1Mlgpeoy72c7b-2FIG-2B8W7cfGANLrsIwLVi1k-2BGX9kvTIFsWcB8LGgcXN5wArHpwuN3tKlYUV0PXLVDikSarWHFRcEwxztnEdE93ajUYlWHL0JgffBtxLZpy35H6Xauo1Yt0FOitg6jX4dUXYxEeEaX5cg5w-2Bmgmy3YkoESVLJXb2VM5XKrSs-2Bmutna1vTcGVv4mHteZYaZd02YNqTiQlXAY5K6vIycJHaaaDeqnnM4sJL60k-2FPE3-2BJgy04oy63PljqsB9ENh2AweILdUcRTRuJK3VcMgGrNiYtsjyhSWiqXaASbRswGltDpgAxMN3VA03-2F8nSXt3gcwwpUvbyftSlC6RxVZROMLpHUXjuIbsBsQ5Q7zIZIO2SK4Kw8VLbrU5TlBR54b0qR0gnYCeWfRmioVckHfMC7UfaEzvQCypJoWD7fR20qn2SYQoThJB9B-2FIMd5YQYrUsACSqz4fMUfC3Q1cwJj7QKctEuOkrEfhLmp5da2gG9fqM90Hk9poHpIvLenwYBkcuxP-2FcTN-2FojplyQiEO19Ap5bDyMzlNjn-2FaDImk7axTtAwsKOyqt6jJJoNgmTnYZgX1NGFClS9K),
a tool for understanding why coal-powered engines were more economically
efficient than earlier wood-powered versions in driving the steam engine that

It was the American agricultural chemist [Wilbur Olin
Atwater](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BGn0rGFLt-2BOrADaTFAxJHgyrLzPV0-2FH89AUsKYz-2FgVn40UT634vhFjBz-2B9BMxsfmnA-3D-3D20im_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BBb8InrSWScXWwwhR8KaNc47rVfyD1XCoa6i59gYLZ9oZIF2-2B57xGvBAIKJX7TG6Hcwua22EO2819LZprpDEx2227d8PHa0Dxn3I1PMgOqFrVkTkNst5jeawcb-2FfLcaeQFqjSrQWI2TK7n1t3tRdydfsyyTzLRZImgGKMmiWc754v-2B2po1Mlgpeoy72c7b-2FIG-2B8W7cfGANLrsIwLVi1k-2BGX9kvTIFsWcB8LGgcXN5wArHpwuN3tKlYUV0PXLVDikSarWHFRcEwxztnEdE93ajUYlWHL0JgffBtxLZpy35H6Xauo1Yt0FOitg6jX4dUXYxEeEaX5cg5w-2Bmgmy3YkoESVLJXb2VM5XKrSs-2Bmutna1vTcGVv4mHteZYaZd02YNqTiQlXAY5K6vIycJHaaaDeqnnM4sJL60k-2FPE3-2BJgy04oy63PljqsB9ENh2AweILdUcRTRuJK3VcMgGrNiYtsjyhSWiqXaASbRswGltDpgAxMN3VA03-2F8nSXt3gcwwpUvbyftSlC6RxVZROMLpHUXjuIbsBsQ5Q7zIZIO2SK4Kw8VK3Aq-2BTov7MSmQ9C-2B-2BTqpVcMebY3ogp-2FxBt-2F9Bwu2J4koFi-2FRJe5cqUpb0XWnOagYpdivqfyNVz3KohUgsU4ezYU2FsmLlAsyE3WgdwvK6gD9YBAB3dFPyCjHR1Q4eRGHOpA-2F4qSA5-2BsiE3dycbHQyqA58PKRHbbU0Kw-2BX-2BBTmvWjKJFjL98aXPlyETExW2HIZVpnG6sCDM-2BCZ3qfyC6htd)
who introduced the concept of calories into the field that would later become
human nutrition. His goal, however, was not just scientific curiosity but was
closely tied to a practical economic question facing the rapidly
industrializing United States. Although the Industrial Revolution had taken
strong hold in America, much work was still performed by people and animals.
The question remained: how could workers, soldiers, laborers, and animals be

Nutritionism gave scientists powerful tools for measuring food, but it also
narrowed the questions being asked. When food is framed as fuel, the central

But living organisms do not experience food as isolated nutrients or abstract
calories. Meals are a part of their daily environmental experience—patterns of
signals interacting with metabolism, microbes, hormones, and behavior over
time.

Understanding those signals requires a different way of thinking about food.

**Nutrients as Biological Signals**

chemical building blocks. Proteins supplied amino acids for tissue growth,
fats stored energy, and formed cellular membranes; carbohydrates fueled

component the body required to function properly.

These findings reveal that biological systems communicate through signals that
can change form as they move across different functional layers of the body.
Microbes may metabolize a dietary fiber molecule into short-chain fatty acids
that influence intestinal cells, which, in turn, send neural and hormonal
signals to the brain. At each step, the signal’s form changes, yet the
underlying message persists.

In some ways, this process resembles downloading music. A singer’s voice
begins as sound waves that are captured by a microphone and converted into
digital data. That information travels across networks as pulses of light
through fiber-optic cables, becomes electromagnetic signals in a router, and
is finally transformed back into sound waves through a phone’s speaker. A
person’s ear converts those vibrations into electrical impulses that the brain
recognizes as a familiar song. The signal’s physical form changes repeatedly,
yet the information remains the same. The song remains the same.

Understanding diet in these terms opens new possibilities for public health.
Rather than focusing exclusively on individual nutrient targets, dietary
guidance may benefit from emphasizing patterns that restore recognizable
biological messages: minimally processed foods, regular meal timing, a
diversity of diets, and social environments that align more closely with the
signals human physiology evolved to interpret.

Seen through this lens, improving population health may depend less on
changing what individuals choose to eat and more on reshaping the
informational structure of the food environment itself.

The emerging science reviewed here suggests that something deeper may be at
work. Food does not simply deliver energy or nutrients. It carries information
interpreted by intertwined biological systems. Health emerges not only from
what we eat but also from how those dietary messages are structured, timed,
and interpreted across these systems.

Our modern food environment has altered the messages we—and the gut microbiome

If we are to meet the diet-related health challenges of the coming decades, we
may need to move beyond nutrient labels and ask a more fundamental question:
what message does this meal convey?

Food—and  _how_ ,_when_ ,_where_ ,_why_ , and  _with whom_ we consume it—may
be one of the most powerful messages shaping health and wellness or disability
and disease.
